title: What Happens When You Open a URL

scenes.line1: What happens when you open a URL?
scenes.say: Ever wonder what really happens when you open a URL? Let’s break it down step by step.

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Browser asks DNS for the server’s IP address.
scenes.say: First, your browser asks the Domain Name System for the server’s IP address.
Next, it sets up a reliable connection with TCP, then secures it using Transport Layer Security for HTTPS.

scenes.title: curl example
scenes.say: Now, your browser sends an HTTP request. It usually hits a load balancer, which forwards it to a backend server.

scenes.question: Does the browser connect directly to the server?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it connects straight to the server.
scenes.right: No, it usually goes through a load balancer first.
scenes.say: Don’t forget: most requests hit a load balancer before reaching the web server. That’s a common interview trap.
